publication_tracks.systems: Offline hair-editing deployment reliability and quality-compute trade-offs
publication_tracks.method: Identity-preserving, reference-conditioned hair synthesis under mobile-browser constraints

research_questions: RQ1: Can browser-local hair editing achieve faithful reference hairstyle transfer with acceptable real-portrait realism and facial identity preservation?
RQ2: Which computational trade-offs dominate Android-browser inference latency, peak memory, and offline reliability?
RQ3: How do head-pose difference, original hairstyle length, and occlusion affect failure rates?

datasets.identity_grouping: Each physical human has a stable study-subject ID independent of filename and image variant

metric_policy.primary_quality: Blinded human paired comparative judgment on hairstyle match, naturalness, facial identity and overall preference, with independent raters
secondary_quality: ArcFace face-identity cosine similarity where valid, reported with bias limitations
systems: peak resident browser memory where measurable
metric_policy.failed_cases: Must remain in denominator and must be reported separately, never omitted silently
metric_policy.fid_kid: Do not use small pilot FID as conclusive proof of photorealism

statistics.multiple_comparisons: Preselect primary comparison; adjust exploratory comparisons or label as exploratory

decision_rules.current_model: MI-GAN generic inpainting, research-only; visual quality no-go
decision_rules.commercial_release: Blocked until checkpoint-lineage license review, real portrait evaluation, and physical Android testing
decision_rules.scientific_publication: Blocked until independent evidence, baseline comparisons, human study and complete reproducibility package
